No.

Torture is not justified, not even in this extreme scenario. While the stakes are undeniably catastrophic—a million lives at risk—justice cannot be achieved at the cost of violating fundamental human rights and the moral fabric upon which a just society is built. Torture is an inherently brutal and unreliable method of interrogation. The information extracted under duress is often false or coerced, rendering the very goal of preventing mass casualties moot. Moreover, legitimizing torture erodes the rule of law and sets a dangerous precedent, opening the door for such practices to be used against vulnerable individuals or for political purposes. In the name of saving lives, we cannot become the very thing we seek to prevent—the source of violence and oppression. True security and justice are found through methods that respect human dignity, uphold the law, and preserve the moral integrity of society.
